doc.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Dizzy Gillespie and Cab Calloway's spitball fight
summary: Doc Cheatham and Dizzy in the band; the spitball incident when Dizzy stuck a knife in Cab's leg. Interviewer hopes Joe Williams and Milt will tell stories.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Wasn’t Doc Cheatham in that band too?
Doc was in the band, Doc had left the band when I was there because Dizzy was there.
If I’m not mistaken I think Dizzy replaced Doc. I’m not sure, don’t quote me, but I think —
I understand Dizzy and Cab had an altercation. Can you tell us that story?

Well, it seemed that they had a little group called the, what was the name of it Cab Jivers. And they would come out and perform. And Dizzy and — I really should let Milton tell that story because he knows the details of it more. But I can remember because a spitball fell in the spotlight. And Cab accused Dizzy of throwing the spitball. And Dizzy was always doing something wrong. But this was one time he was right. He really hadn’t thrown the spitball, and I’m not going to go into detail to explain who did throw it, because he never admitted that he threw it, but everyone knew who it was. Yeah, and Cab and Dizzy had this little scuffle and Dizzy stuck his knife in Cab’s leg, and I think Milton broke it up. And then Benny Payne and Chu Berry and some of the others came and, as Milton calls them, Pachyderms, they came and broke it up. But Cab and Dizzy, they became friends, I mean they didn’t hold grudges for a long time. But as I say I should let Milton tell that story because he knows, and you know Milton is a great storyteller anyway.

Well we intend to get Milton in this series, don’t worry, but what we would like to do is have Joe Williams do it. Because Joe and Milton I’ve heard them together and they’re unbelievable, the stories they tell.
Well they go back a long time from when they were youngsters in Chicago.
